title: Continuous transfinite towers of categorical fibrations compute coherent limits
statement: Use the universes, simplicial sets, quasicategories, coherent diagrams, cores and mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and isofibrations of [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation]. Use $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ and the coherent diagram associated to a strict diagram as defined in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], in a containing universe. Fix a small nonzero ordinal $\lambda$ and a strict inverse diagram $X:\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathsf{sSet}$ of small quasicategories. Assume that $X_{\alpha+1}\to X_\alpha$ is an isofibration whenever $\alpha+1<\lambda$, and that, for every nonzero limit ordinal $\beta<\lambda$, the canonical map $X_\beta\to\lim_{\alpha<\beta}X_\alpha$ is a simplicial isomorphism. Then the degreewise simplicial limit $L=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}X_\alpha$ is a quasicategory and its projection cone is a limit cone in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. For every small simplicial set $K$, the canonical equality $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X_\alpha)$ presents a limit in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ as well. These comparisons are induced by projections and are natural in maps of continuous inverse diagrams and restrictions of $K$. No surjectivity on objects is assumed.

source.place: Appendix A.2.9, especially Proposition A.2.9.19, Example A.2.9.22, and Corollaries A.2.9.24(ii) and A.2.9.25(2): well-founded inverse Reedy diagrams and injective fibrancy. The statement is the agent-formulated continuous-ordinal specialization in the Joyal model, extending the sequential case of Kerodon Example 7.6.5.10 (03HT), read online. No Stacks tag states this result; archival copy WANTED.

proof.text: Put $I=\lambda^{\mathrm{op}}$ and let $\mathcal M$ be the Joyal model category of [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. Apply [lem-coef-ordinal-inverse-diagram-model] to $\mathcal M$ and this small ordinal. Its matching object at $\alpha$ is $M_\alpha X=\lim_{\gamma<\alpha}X_\gamma$. At $0$ the matching map is $X_0\to\Delta^0$, a Joyal fibration since $X_0$ is a quasicategory. At a successor $\alpha+1$, the earlier diagram has initial index $\alpha$, so its cones are uniquely specified by the component at $\alpha$; hence $M_{\alpha+1}X=X_\alpha$ canonically. The matching map is the assumed isofibration. Clause (1) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations], with exactly the equivalence-edge lifting condition used in [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], makes it a Joyal fibration. At a nonzero limit the matching map is a simplicial isomorphism by continuity, hence a fibration (transport any lifting square through its inverse). These exhaust the indices, so $X$ is fibrant in this diagram model structure. No natural-number degree restriction is being used.

source.place: Paragraph 2, inverse-limit infrastructure: ordinal matching-object check; general model input is HTT A.2.9.19 and A.2.9.24(ii), recorded in the cited ordinal-model node.

proof.text: The constant-diagram functor $c:\mathcal M\to\mathcal M^I$ has right adjoint the strict limit: a natural map $cT\to D$ is a compatible family of maps $T\to D_\alpha$, so factors uniquely through $\lim_I D$. The model structure of [lem-coef-ordinal-inverse-diagram-model] makes cofibrations and trivial cofibrations objectwise. Thus $c$ preserves both classes. By [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction], its right adjoint preserves fibrations. It preserves the terminal object as well: a compatible family in the constant terminal diagram is unique. Apply it to the fibrant diagram $X$ of Step 1. Its strict limit $L$ is fibrant in $\mathcal M$, hence a quasicategory by [lem-coef-joyal-model-structure]. The ordinary counit $cL\to X$ has precisely the stated simplicial projections as its components.

source.place: Paragraph 2, derived coefficient adjunction before the inverse limit: constant/strict-limit adjunction and its Quillen class check.

proof.text: Let $W$ be the Joyal weak equivalences and $W_I$ their objectwise class. Write $\mathcal C=\mathcal M[W^{-1}]_\infty$ and $\mathcal D=\mathcal M^I[W_I^{-1}]_\infty$. The constant functor preserves all weak equivalences, so [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] identifies its left derived functor with its directly localized functor $\bar c$. All simplicial sets are cofibrant because initial inclusions are monomorphisms, and $X$ is already fibrant by Step 1. Thus the derived right functor at $q_I X$ is represented by the exact object $L=\lim_I X$, with counit represented by the projection transformation $cL\to X$. The derived adjunction gives, for every object $T$ of $\mathcal C$, a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,qL)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(\bar cT,q_I X)$. It is the map obtained by applying $\bar c$ and then composing with that counit. Hence this equivalence retains the cone, not merely its apex.

source.place: Paragraph 2, displayed R Hom / R lim adjunction: coherent derived adjunction including its counit, applied to a fibrant inverse diagram.

proof.text: [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification] applies, $\mathcal M$ being a model category with functorial factorizations and $I$ small. $\Theta_I$ identifies $\mathcal D$ with $\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal C)$, carrying $q_IX$ to $q\circ N(X)$, the localized constants to the coherent constants and the counit of Step 3 to the image of the projection cone. Step 3 becomes $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(T,qL)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(N(I),\mathcal C)}(\Delta T,q\circ N(X))$, given by composition with that cone, so by the mapping-space criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] the image of the projection cone is limiting in $\mathcal C$. Pass to $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration] by the derived coherent-nerve identification of [lem-coef-coherent-nerve-comparison], computed on objects and strict maps by $Q\mapsto N_{\mathrm{hc}}R\mathfrak C[Q]$; equivalences preserve limiting cones by the same criterion. For a quasicategory $Q$ the unit $\eta_Q:Q\to N_{\mathrm{hc}}R\mathfrak C[Q]$ is adjunct to the Dwyer--Kan equivalence $\mathfrak C[Q]\to R\mathfrak C[Q]$, whose target is locally Kan, hence Bergner fibrant; as $Q$ is Joyal cofibrant, the Quillen-equivalence clause makes $\eta_Q$ a categorical equivalence of quasicategories, natural in strict maps. By clause (2) of [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations] each $\eta_{X_\alpha}$ and $\eta_L$ is an equivalence in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. The strict cone $cL\to X$ is a strict diagram on the ordinary category $I^{\triangleleft}$; the coherent nerve of an ordinary category is its ordinary nerve, so $\eta$ is a coherent transformation between its coherent nerve diagram, as specified in [def-cbc-enhanced-cartesian-fibration], and the transported cone. By the vertex-component clause of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] it is an equivalence of cones. Hence the projection cone with apex $L$ is limiting in this exact $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$.

source.place: Paragraph 2, passage from the derived inverse limit to a coherent limit: ordinary-diagram rectification, Joyal--Bergner comparison, and the coherent cone criterion.

proof.text: For every simplicial degree $n$, the internal functor object of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and the degreewise limit give $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)_n=\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,L)=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,X_\alpha)=\lim_{\alpha<\lambda}\operatorname{Fun}(K,X_\alpha)_n$. A map into a degreewise limit is exactly a compatible family, so these are canonical identifications. They commute with the operators induced by maps of standard simplices, and assemble to the asserted equality of simplicial sets. The same calculation applies to any initial segment of the tower.

source.place: Paragraph 2, functoriality of the inverse limit: degreewise compatible-family calculation of the internal Hom.

proof.text: Set $Y_\alpha=\operatorname{Fun}(K,X_\alpha)$. By [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] these are quasicategories. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation] to each successor transition with $A=\varnothing$ and $B=K$. Since $\operatorname{Fun}(\varnothing,-)=\Delta^0$, the corner map is exactly $Y_{\alpha+1}\to Y_\alpha$, so it is an isofibration. At every nonzero limit stage, Step 5 identifies the comparison $Y_\beta\to\lim_{\alpha<\beta}Y_\alpha$ with the internal Hom of the given simplicial isomorphism, hence an isomorphism. Thus $Y$ has all the hypotheses used for the arbitrary tower $X$ in Steps 1--4. Applying that argument to $Y$ proves that its strict limit is its limit in $\mathrm{Cat}_\infty$. By Step 5 that strict limit and its cone are $\operatorname{Fun}(K,L)$ and the images of the original projections.

source.place: Paragraph 2, retained coherent parameters in the inverse-limit adjunction: exponentiated tower and the same derived-limit argument.

proof.text: For a strict map of continuous inverse diagrams $a:X\to X'$, the limit map sends the compatible family $(x_\alpha)$ to $(a_\alpha x_\alpha)$, and $\pi_\alpha\lim(a)=a_\alpha\pi_\alpha$ in every simplicial degree. For $K'\to K$, precomposition on $\operatorname{Hom}(K\times\Delta^n,-)$ commutes with every projection and with the compatible-family identification of Step 5. These identities give the stated naturality of comparisons and cones; the coherent versions retain these transformations by the naturality clauses of [lem-coef-model-infinity-derived-adjunction] and [lem-coef-small-diagram-model-rectification]. No stage used surjectivity on objects. Empty stages and $K=\varnothing$ are permitted.

source.place: Paragraph 2, last paragraph: specified maps and naturality retained by the derived-limit calculation.

proof_origin.place: Paragraph 2, displayed derived Hom/inverse-limit calculation. Agent-written ordinal matching-object and coherent derived-adjunction specialization from the cited DAG statements; the new general diagram-model input is separately stated, not used as a bare URL theorem.
